rules.sentence: Patent foramen ovale and atrial septal defect represent functionally similar pathologies; however, they differ in their etiology as well as clinical severity.

Atrial septal defects may undergo spontaneous closure depending on their initial size at the time of diagnosis, found to be the best predictor of the progression of such defects.
Holes in the fossa ovalis measuring less than 8mm and/or containing aneurysms may diminish in size or resolve spontaneously.[16][17]
However, failure of closure usually leads to enlargement of the defect and the need for surgical closure.[16][18]
